chunks: He said and Abdullah ibn Salam narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
Among the inevitable matters is that this son of mine is the Qaim of this Ummah and the owner of the sword; and he pointed with his hand to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him).

key_terms.صَاحِبُ السَّيْفِ: The owner of the sword (symbolizing authority and leadership)
key_terms.قَائِمُ: The Rising One / The one who rises to establish justice

ai.seo_question: Who is the Qaim of the Ummah according to Imam al-Sadiq in this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* serves as a crucial proof for the Waqifiyya sect, who halted their belief in the Imamate after Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.), by explicitly identifying him as the 'Qaim' and 'Sahib al-Sayf' (Master of the Sword). The designation 'Sahib al-Sayf' highlights his dual role as both a spiritual leader and the political authority who will rise to fill the earth with justice, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatology.
